title: The creator economy’s stance on AI is shifting — again
tldr: Creators are embedding AI tools into their workflows, but there's growing anxiety about creative sameness when AI overtakes the process. A real tension between efficiency and distinctiveness.
why_fresh: documents an active shift in creator sentiment
angle: Why 'sameness' is the real AI risk for creators — and how human quirk becomes the moat.

title: When everyone has AI, being human becomes the competitive advantage
tldr: Argues that as AI commoditizes content production, human judgment, voice and connection become the differentiator. Directly aligned with human-centered content thinking.
angle: The 'humanity premium': auditing your content for what only a person could have made.

title: What therapists say about this new antidote for doomscrolling—‘bloomscrolling’
tldr: 'Bloomscrolling' — intentionally seeking uplifting content — reflects a broader shift away from passive negative consumption. A real signal in how people consume media.
angle: What 'bloomscrolling' means for brands: designing content for the mood people want to be in.

title: The ‘Twitter killers’ never replaced Twitter. Here’s what happened instead.
tldr: A clear-eyed status check on Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon and X — no single winner emerged, and audiences fragmented. Useful for platform strategy decisions.
angle: Fragmentation is the new normal: how to build owned audiences when no town square exists.

title: When Men Use AI, They’re Resourceful. When Women Use AI, They’re Cheating.
tldr: Gini Dietrich walks through three studies showing women are trusted less than men for identical AI use. A sharp, research-backed communications issue.
why_fresh: new research angle on AI perception bias
angle: The AI credibility gap: how perception bias shapes who gets to use the tools openly.

title: How publishers are rethinking audience engagement: Five takeaways from the Future of Media Technology Conference
tldr: Practical takeaways from publishers on shifting engagement strategies in the AI era. Concrete and current from a notable industry gathering.
angle: What publisher engagement experiments can teach brand content teams.

title: How Thorne built a brand platform ahead of $3.8B P&G deal — and what’s next
tldr: A detailed breakdown of how Thorne turned consumer insights into campaigns and a distinct communication style that drove a major acquisition. A real campaign case study.
angle: How a communication style — not just a product — can drive enterprise value.

title: The engagement survey is dying. Here’s what’s replacing it

angle: From annual survey theater to always-on listening: what internal comms should own.

angle: Restructuring content ops for AI: lessons from Expedia's six moves.
